title: Deep-learning seismic picks reveal upper-mantle upwelling conduits beneath Southwestern US volcanic fields
summary: Using an expanded Pn-wave travel-time database, the authors construct a high-resolution uppermost-mantle velocity and anisotropy model for the southwestern United States. The tomographic interpretation identifies separate low-velocity, anisotropic upwelling conduits beneath the Black Rock Desert, Uinkaret, and San Francisco volcanic fields along the Colorado Plateau margins, and supports remnants of the ancient Farallon slab beneath the central Great Basin.
organization: Institute of Geology and Geophysics, Chinese Academy of Sciences; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences; Shandong Earthquake Agency

evidence.tested: Using an expanded Pn-wave travel-time database, the authors construct a high-resolution uppermost-mantle velocity and anisotropy model for the southwestern United States.
evidence.unknown: These are tomographic interpretations of seismic velocity and anisotropy, not direct images or direct measurements of magma conduits. The article abstract reports inferred independent thermal upwellings and supports (rather than proves uniquely) Farallon slab remnants. Resolution and tectonic interpretation depend on the travel-time picks and inversion assumptions; the paper's abstract does not establish direct volcanic plumbing connectivity.
evidence.ai_role: The authors used Seis-PickNet to automatically pick Pn phases and expand the regional travel-time database; those new picks underpin the velocity and anisotropy tomography from which the mantle structures are interpreted. The AI supplies the expanded seismic measurements used in the scientific inversion, rather than only classifying existing results.
